author: Mike Kasberg
units: mm assumed; corroborated by source sheet dimensions, STL contains no units

designDecisions.adaptation: Two cheeks, cam, flat axle and keeper preserve 1.6 mm sheet stock. Deck independently strengthened to 2–2.8 mm.

designDecisions.measured: Actual mesh socket loops 4.5 x 1.700012 mm
designDecisions.adaptation: 4.4 mm tongue with .10 mm total allowance reconstructs measured slot. Default .15 mm and .10–.35 mm range are proposed printer/material-dependent fits. Four deck sockets require adhesive.

designDecisions.measured: Low .21/.22 mm runners and multi-bay source carrier
designDecisions.adaptation: Original 3x2 carrier with 24 accessible .4–.6 mm thick runners; safe snip positions tested to release six parts plus frame. Axle tabs moved onto unobstructed head lands after independent snip test caught shaft interference.

designDecisions.original: Arched cheeks, eccentric cam, round bearings and flat headed axle
designDecisions.adaptation: Cam R12–15, eccentricity2–3, 1.6 mm sheet thickness, 10–16 mm lever. Bore radius hypot(axleWidth/2,.8)+.25. Axis height deck+R+e+.5. Half-turn[-90,90] yields .5 to .5+2e nominal nip. 14 x7 cheek arches admit paper strips/edges. No sprung follower or repeated prior kit assembly.

designDecisions.original: Positive head/keeper capture after adhesive cure
designDecisions.adaptation: 10 mm broad head and 10x10 keeper overlap round bores by >=1.64 mm. Keeper slides over flat axle and must be bonded. .35 mm endplay per cheek outside face. No unsupported friction-retention claim.

6 mm default footprint, engraving .4–.6; mark at X0,Y=-deckLength/2+14. Exact imported convex STL Boolean subtraction or 20x20 image-height surface. Rotated/shifted art bounded to6.5 mm safe radius, preserves >=1.4 mm deck backing, stays outside sockets.

sourceDefects: 27 edge-adjacent components, nonwatertight. Used as design reference only; original CSG reconstruction, no automatic repair.
novelty: Six-sheet assembly converts manual eccentric turning into a variable paper nip through open arches. It is not the earlier Camber spring-follower fidget or the wedge-driven miniature press; no source ship outlines are copied. Shared studio/import/test infrastructure is adapted, mechanism solids and assembly checks are original.
